It takes real strength to keep searching for something that helps, especially after years of trying and feeling let down by therapists. That exhaustion is understandable, and it doesn't mean you're broken or beyond help—it may mean the right fit or approach hasn't come along yet.

Sometimes what works isn't one big coping skill but a few small things layered together, or an approach like DBT that's specifically designed for self-harm. If past therapists haven't clicked, it can help to ask directly about their experience with self-harm, or to try a different style. You deserve support that actually meets you where you are.

If you ever feel close to seriously hurting yourself, please reach out right away—call or text 988 (in the US) or go to your nearest emergency room. You don't have to get through those moments alone. Is there a small step you'd feel okay taking this week?
